title: Equilibrium in continuous time

prereqs.why: The condition is pi G = 0, not pi P = pi, and getting that right is most of the exercise.
The generator collects the jump rates, with each diagonal entry minus the sum of its row.
The discrete-time analogue is what the equation has to be distinguished from.

statement:
A continuous-time Markov chain on $\{a, b, c\}$ has generator

$$G = \begin{pmatrix}
-2 & 2 & 0\\
1 & -3 & 2\\
0 & 3 & -3
\end{pmatrix}$$

with rows and columns in the order $a, b, c$. The off-diagonal entry
$g_{i,j}$ is the rate of jumps from $i$ to $j$, and each diagonal entry is
minus the sum of the rest of its row.

The chain is irreducible and finite, hence non-explosive and positive
recurrent, so it has a unique stationary distribution $\pi$, characterised by

$$\pi G = 0, \qquad \sum_i \pi_i = 1 .$$

Give $\pi_b$ exactly.
hints: $\pi G = 0$ means $\sum_i \pi_i g_{i,j} = 0$ for each $j$ — a sum down **column** $j$ of $G$.
Column $a$ involves only two entries, because $g_{c,a} = 0$. Start there: it gives $\pi_b$ in terms of $\pi_a$ at once.
Column $c$ is also short: $2\pi_b - 3\pi_c = 0$. Between the two you can write everything in terms of $\pi_a$.
As in discrete time, one of the three equations is redundant. Use two of them and the normalisation.

payload.label: $\pi_b =$
payload.syntax: A number or a fraction. Arithmetic is fine.
